answer: Sybil resistance works like a toll on a river: each agent must lock a bond, real value, before it may vote or earn. One identity needs one bond, so an attacker wanting a thousand voices must pay a thousand bonds. The cost rises with every fake identity, while honest agents reclaim their stake through work. If a validator catches double-voting, that bond is slashed and burned. Think of a lantern on a lonely island: its light is trusted only because someone paid for the fuel, and a copycat cannot glow in every place at once without paying for every lamp.
